sourceAgencies: Woodland Park Borough Governing Body & School District Collective Bargaining Agreements
Passaic County Joint Insurance Fund (JIF) / Municipal Employee Benefits Fund
NJ Division of Pensions and Benefits (SHBP / SEHBP)

overview.percentageOfCombinedBudgets: 18.3% of all public spending in Woodland Park Borough goes to employee healthcare and state pensions

healthcarePlans.providers: State Health Benefits Program (SHBP) / Municipal Joint Insurance Fund (JIF) & SEHBP

primaryPlans.planName: Woodland Park Borough Municipal Direct Access / JIF Healthcare
primaryPlans.description: Comprehensive network medical coverage for full-time municipal civil service employees, police, and DPW personnel.

primaryPlans.planName: NJ Educators Health Plan (NJEHP / Chapter 44) & Garden State Plan
primaryPlans.description: Mandated school district health plan for certified teachers and support educators in Woodland Park Borough Public Schools.
Retail, mail-order, and maintenance prescription drug coverage with taxpayers subsidizing 80%+ of pharmacy expenses.
Preventive, restorative dental and vision benefits for eligible full-time municipal and school staff.

rules.tier: Woodland Park Borough Municipal Staff & Police (Chapter 78 Tier 4 Grid)
rules.employeeContribution: 10% to 35% of premium based on salary tier
rules.taxpayerContribution: 65% to 90% of total family premium ($22,000 - $32,000/yr subsidy)
rules.note: For an employee with family coverage, Woodland Park Borough taxpayers subsidize ~$24,000+ per year.

rules.tier: Woodland Park Borough School Educators (Chapter 44 NJEHP)
rules.note: Because educator contributions are capped by salary percentage, annual health insurance premium increases fall directly onto the local school property tax levy.

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Employees retiring with 25+ years of credited pensionable service receive employer-paid health coverage until Medicare eligibility, plus Medicare Part B reimbursement.

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.legalAuthority: NJ Division of Pensions and Benefits (N.J.S.A. 43:16A & 43:15A)
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Mandatory municipal employer contributions to Police & Firemen's Retirement System (PFRS) and Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS). School district teachers participate in Teachers' Pension and Annuity Fund (TPAF).

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.benefitName: Accumulated Sick Leave & Terminal Leave Payouts
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.taxpayerImpact: Capped at $15,000 for post-2010 hires; legacy liabilities for veteran staff
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Under N.J.S.A. 11A:6-19.2, terminal sick leave payouts are capped at $15,000 for staff hired after May 2010. Legacy personnel retain contractually grandfathered bank hours.
